cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Then there's more. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. I'll call. It's Mum's old bakery. I want you there when I tell her.

mechanism: A treats its pupil successful protection of family privacy as earned advancement to more sensitive personal news, then accepts B better communication judgment.
confusable: Not dumping all secrets at once: each B act of discretion earns a more vulnerable disclosure and greater trust.
comparison: Behavioral secrecy test versus secure conversational channel and family revelation.
